mutant.description: The producer's book aggregation was mutated by REMOVING the supervision-sleeve term from its key -- reverting to (group, account) and keeping one row, which is the form both this producer and the T1 oracle originally shipped.
mutant.expected: If the sleeve term is load-bearing, group books must move, because an account split Supervised/Unsupervised would contribute only one of its two sleeves.
mutant.observed: FIRED. 12 of 201 group books change, total understatement $24,605,360.68 -- Austin Thompson, Lane Curry - Local Ops and Ted Grant each +$3,657,307.24; Collin Plotts +$3,159,412.24; Sydney Cobb, Patrick Mundlin and Campbell Huber each +$2,887,004.52; Hunter Lloyd and Sam Owens - Local Ops each +$497,895.00; 49F Schwab AUM, Christopher Spalthoff - Local Ops and Lane Curry each +$272,407.72. The correction is PROVEN, not assumed: for every sleeve, account_market_value / account_allocation == portfolio_group_market_value to the cent, i.e. both sleeves divide the SAME portfolio total, positive-controlled against an ordinary single-sleeve account; and the corrected key has constant market value on 29,926 of 29,926 keys, zero exceptions. The same mutant re-run against the T1 sibling moved 79 of 201 groups, |delta| $206,733,899.92. SEPARATELY, A COLLAPSE-SAFETY ASSERTION WAS ADDED at DS base's prompting and it is a distinct hazard from the sleeve one: the book key (group, account, supervised) is NOT unique -- the dual-fee-schedule account z0813542821 carries two simultaneous schedules (100bps and 125bps) and so puts 2 rows on that key in each of its 5 groups. Its market value is CONSTANT across them, so COLLAPSE-TAKE-ONE is correct and SUM WOULD DOUBLE-COUNT (47,014.32 per group against a true 23,507.16). MEASURED, not reasoned: rows surviving dedup in its group = 1, and the group 'Neil Tjon-Hing' books $22,479,576.71 on BOTH the oracle and the T2 producer. assert_book_key_collapsible() now pins the property the collapse depends on and fails LOUD if a future edit switches to SUM or the vendor makes the value non-constant; it holds on 29,926 keys. 'Constant within key' and 'safe to sum' are DIFFERENT properties and this key satisfies only the first.
